Inglewood, California
  April 6, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 6, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas, other than the Public Hearing.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item No. O-1,
  adoption of Ordinance No. 21-06, to define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand the hours
  when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and update of job titles.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item No. O-1, adoption of Ordinance
  No. 21-06, to define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand the hours when people are
  prohibited from being in City Parks, and update of job titles.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item No. O-1,
  adoption of Ordinance No. 21-06, to define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand the hours
  when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and update of job titles. He also
  suggested equipping the Police Officers with body cameras.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, received emails regarding Agenda Item No. O-1,
  adoption of Ordinance No. 21-06, to define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand the hours
  when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and update of job titles from the
  following: Violeta Reinaga, Betty J. White, Cassie Faulding, Michelle Munsat, Tieira
  (Last Name Unknown), Jon Goncalves, Kaylee Bieraugel, Brett Matich, Alexis Aceves,
  Suraiya Prasla, Madalena Burke, Eliza Sanchez, and Professor Cynthia Guardado.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April
  1, 2021, in the amount of $2,952,315.08, and March 26, 2021, in the amount of
  $1,690,562.91 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:

  1
 April 6, 2021

  Ayes:  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  183  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 21-07 INTRODUCED-
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2 (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE (INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT). The
  City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider an
  ordinance amending Chapter 2 (Administration) of the Inglewood Municipal Code,
  notice had been given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was
  on file, and no communication were received.

  Louis Atwell, Public Works Director/ Assistant City Manager, introduced the presenter.

  Lisa Trifiletti, Project Manager for the Inglewood Transit Connector, presented the staff
  report and an update of the ITC Project, which included the approval of the Joint Powers
  Authority Agreement. She also stated that an Industry Forum was held with over 300
  people and one-on-one interviews with over 16 different industry partners interested in
  the project. She further said they’re looking at the same delivery structure that Los
  Angeles Airport used for their automated people mover. Ms. Trifiletti referenced
  information is contained in the staff report on this matter.

  Council Member Padilla thanked Lisa Trifiletti for helping District 2 get the information
  out to the residents in Spanish and English. He stated the information was included in the
  Newsletters for District 2 residents, which had the project's process and the projected
  length of completion. Council Member Padilla mentioned concerns regarding the
  project's impact on Market Street, but all concerns were addressed in the information
  given to the residents.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning a matter unrelated to the Public Hearing, and
  was advised to call back towards the end of the meeting.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding the lack of transparency regarding the project.
  She mentioned the date of the report for the project was made available two days before
  Christmas when City Hall was shut down. She requested that the City Council focus on
  improving streets and transportation and address issues she faced as an eleven-year
  resident.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, suggested the Public Hearings be held at 7:00 p.m., and
  Ordinance No. 16-01, which allows the Mayor to set the City Council Meeting times.
  Mr. Mathieu also spoke about Article 32, Section 1, of the City Charter, which feels
  obsolete.

  Eddie Cruz, called but the phone call dropped.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-07 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ADDING
  SECTION 2-196.1 INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROCUREMENTS
  TO ARTICLE 5 OF CHAPTER 2 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE
  AUTHORIZING USE OF ALTERNATIVE PROJECT DELIVERY METHODS
  AND ESTABLISHING CERTAIN REQUIREMENTS FOR PROCUREMENTS

  2
 April 6, 2021

  AND CONTRACTS RELATED TO THE PROPOSED INGLEWOOD
  TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Teresa Fonseca for alleged property damage on February 11, 2021.
  2) Sheron Howard for alleged personal injury on June 20, 2020.
  3) Inether Smith for alleged personal injury on August 28, 2020.
  4) Stephanie Smith for alleged property damage on January 7, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A1 through A4. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  171  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-238 APPROVED – SIRSI
  CORPORATION. Staff report dated April 6, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-238 with Sirsi Corporation for the
  Implementation of an Integrated Library Software System.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-
  238 with Sirsi Corporation to add the Blue Cloud Mobile App to the current integrated
  library software system for $20,410; and 2) Approve an increase in the previously
  approved contingency of $13,460 to a new total contingency of $26,920 to allow for the
  purchase of future complementary products and services during the five (5)-year
  agreement period. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 16-142 APPROVED - LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY.
  Staff report dated April 6, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment
  No. 1 to Agreement No. 16-142 with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA) for Sub-regional Paratransit Services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 16-
  142 with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) for
  Sub-Regional Paratransit Services and to add a new Section 8 (Cares Act Funding); and
  2) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1 on behalf of the City of Inglewood.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT FOUR OF THE ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM SERVICES
  SUBAWARD NO. ENP202107 APPROVED - LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE
  DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES (WDACS). Staff report
  dated April 6, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment Four
  (Families First Coronavirus Response Act Grant Funding Reallocation) to the Elderly
  Nutrition Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment Four of the Elderly Nutrition
  Program Services Subaward Number ENP202107 with the County of Los Angeles
  Workforce Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to reflect award of
  additional funding for provision of the Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of
  $105,101. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

  3
 April 6, 2021

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-133 APPROVED - MURPHY’S BOWL, LLC;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-79 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET; CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-134
  APPROVED – LAYNE CHRISTENSEN COMPANY. Staff report dated April 6,
  2021, was presented recommending approval of an Advance Funding Agreement with
  Murphy’s Bowl, LLC and award a construction contract for the Inglewood New Well No.
  8 construction project (Bid No. CB-21-03).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-133 with Murphy’s
  Bowl, LLC (Developer) to fund the construction of Inglewood New Well No. 8 in the
  total amount of $3,687,114.20 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the amount
  of $335,192.20; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-79 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO RECEIVE
  FUNDING TO CONSTRUCT WELL NUMBER 8

  and; 3) Award a contract and approve Agreement No. 21-134 with Layne Christensen
  Company (Contractor) to provide construction services in an amount not to exceed
  $3,687,114.20 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the amount of $335,192.20.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-135 APPROVED – ALL
  AMERICAN ASPHALT. Staff report dated April 6 2021, was presented recommending
  award of a contract and approval of an agreement with All American Asphalt.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby award a construction contract and approve Agreement
  No. 21-135 with All American Asphalt in an amount not to exceed $2,477,272 (includes
  a fifteen percent (15%) project contingency not to exceed $323,122) for the Fiscal Year
  2020-2021 Street and Alley Improvements Project, per Bid No. CB-20-10. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  ORDINANCE NO. 21-06 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 5-67 TO: DEFINE THE TERMS “CAMP OR
  LODGE,” EXPAND HOURS WHEN PEOPLE ARE PROHIBITED FROM
  BEING IN CITY PARKS, AND UPDATE JOB TITLES. Staff report dated April 6
  2021, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 21-06, amending the
  Inglewood Municipal Code (I.M.C.) Section 5-67 (Unauthorized Use of Park Facilities
  Prohibited) to: define the terms “camp or lodge,” expand hours when people are
  prohibited from being in City Parks, and update job titles.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that Ordinance No. 21-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE SECTION 5-67 TO DEFINE THE TERM “CAMP OR LODGE,”

  4
 April 6, 2021

  EXPAND THE HOURS WHEN PEOPLE ARE PROHIBITED FROM BEING
  IN THE CITY PARKS, AND UPDATE JOB TITLES

  which was introduced at the meeting held on March 23, 2021, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported emails received from Oscar Sandoval, Antonio
  Preciado, Marisol Medina, and Claudia Haro-Contreras in support of Assembly Bill
  1163, using the revenue from existing revenue soda taxes to provide direct assistance to
  low-income communities of color. She also reported an email received from Marvin
  McCoy, who requested Public Records of future payments of legal bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on Brown Act Violations, specifically the time limits
  allowed to speak on Agenda Items, personal safety issues, unprofessional behavior of the
  Inglewood Police Department, and the naming of the Fairview Heights Apartments.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item O-1, adoption of Ordinance No.
  21-06, expansion of hours when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and
  updated job titles.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke against the time set for City Council Meetings and asked
  how to obtain the Minutes for the City Council Meetings on the website.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke against the time set for the City Council Meetings and
  equipping the Police with cameras.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item O-1, adoption of Ordinance No.
  21-06, expansion of hours when people are prohibited from being in City Parks, and
  updated job titles.

  Cynthia Guardado, College Professor, commented on Agenda Item O-1, adoption of
  Ordinance No. 21-06, expansion of hours when people are prohibited from being in City
  Parks, and updated job titles. She also requested her email to be read.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at 2:40 p.m.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Ramiro Centeno, at the hour of 2:50 p.m.

  Approved this 10th day of August, 2021.
